page: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the c5.2xlarge consistently in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the middle 50% of tested servers, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1175.0 and a multi-core score of 4531.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 437.77 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 50.41 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The server exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing, which fall into the bottom 25% of benchmarks. Large language model inference speeds are also limited, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model falling into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of bundled local storage. It is well-suited for compute-bound applications such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 7.26 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a Redis SET performance of 7.77 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include software compilation, text processing, and moderate physics simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server utilizing the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor. Operating at 3.4 GHz, this x86_64 instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and is paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It does not feature local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark results position the c5.2xlarge in the average tier for general compute, memory bandwidth, and web serving, though it shows weaker performance in multi-threaded decompression and LLM inference. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for dedicated CPU-bound tasks, making it suitable for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and standard database operations.
